thesis: Corcept reported Q2 2026 revenue of $256.1M, up 32% year over year — Korlym and its authorised generic contributed $208.6M and newly launched Lifyorli $47.6M in its first quarter of availability — and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.1-1.2B; reported diluted EPS was $0.36 against roughly $0.01 modeled. Lifyorli uptake was disclosed as more than 1,300 patients treated, over 1,000 prescribing physicians and coverage for more than 70% of relevant insured lives. The strongest counter-evidence is the Korlym patent dispute with Teva: a District Court ruled in December 2023 that Teva's proposed generic would not infringe, and Corcept's Federal Circuit appeal was argued in July 2025 — this run could not confirm the appeal's current status, and Korlym still accounts for roughly 81% of quarterly revenue, so an adverse outcome would bear directly on the majority of the disclosed revenue base. That risk is not resolved by anything found this run, which is why this is not rated high; the disclosed print itself is a clean beat-and-raise rather than mixed evidence. A separate insider sale of about $1.85M by the Chief Development Officer on 10 August was also disclosed. Shares sit 3.4% below the 52-week high, which is what tripped the screen alongside a 48% 60-day move.
invalidation: Full-year guidance is walked back below the $1.1B floor, Lifyorli prescription growth stalls in the next quarterly disclosure, or the Federal Circuit affirms non-infringement in a way the company says will allow generic Korlym entry.
sources: Corcept Therapeutics Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR, Teva litigation status): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1088856/000162828025037005/cort-20250630.htm

thesis: Marvell is down about 30% over the 60-day window and roughly 37% from its prior high, but the reporting this run found attributes the decline to a sector-wide rotation out of high-multiple AI and semiconductor names and to rising Treasury yields raising the financing cost of AI infrastructure, not to any company-disclosed deterioration — one report explicitly notes a bullish UBS AI note was swamped by the yield move. No company-specific negative catalyst was confirmed; the most recent company figure found was 28% year-over-year revenue growth, and the next binary event is the 27 August earnings report, which is pending rather than disclosed. The counter-case for buying the dip is exactly that growth record, but nothing this run read settles whether the multiple compression is finished ahead of that print. This suggests waiting for the disclosed result rather than entering into an unresolved macro repricing days before earnings.
invalidation: The 27 August results and guidance are delivered and the stock's reaction establishes a company-specific rather than sector-wide read.

thesis: Sandisk is down 28.5% over the 60-day window after an extraordinary round trip — a fall of about 56% from a 25 June closing high of $2,335.00 to $1,015.89 on 29 July, then a partial recovery, with the stock slipping back below $1,700 today. Secondary reporting cites Q2 revenue of $8.97B, EPS of $39.25 against $33.28 expected and non-GAAP gross margin of 84.6%, but this run did not read a company release or filing stating those figures, so the print is treated as unconfirmed rather than as a beat. The same reporting attributes the volatility to profit-taking and sentiment shifts rather than fundamental deterioration, and notes Sandisk's 50.7% quarterly growth lagged the top five memory makers. Evidence that the moves are sentiment-driven, combined with figures this run could not verify at source, leaves no clear net read; 50%+ drawdowns and recoveries inside two months are not an entry this pipeline can time.
invalidation: A company release or filing confirms the quarterly figures and the stock's realised volatility narrows enough that a position could survive a normal stop.

thesis: Corning is down 23.8% over the 60-day window. Three separate drivers turned up and none is a company-disclosed deterioration: the stock fell about 12% on 28 July after its earnings report, leading a broader rout in optical names; it fell again in August on a Jefferies supply-chain report that Apple had scrapped a planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone previously scheduled for a September 2027 launch — a third-party research claim, not a Corning or Apple disclosure; and it fell about 8% today in a sector-wide optics selloff that reporting describes as largely macro in origin, with nothing changed in the underlying indium phosphide picture in 24 hours. Insiders sold $36.7M over the last three months with no reported buying. The counter-case is that the stock remains up roughly 80-98% year to date on intact AI-optics demand, but a decline driven by a sourced-but-unconfirmed customer report plus a risk-off rotation is sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental change, and this run cannot separate the two.
invalidation: Corning or Apple confirms or denies the all-glass iPhone cancellation, or Corning's next disclosure quantifies the specialty-glass demand impact.

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 2026 on 6 August with a fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue, $191.9M, up 86% year over year on AI datacentre optics and CATV demand, and EPS of $0.06 against $0.01 expected; management guided Q3 revenue to $255-290M and adjusted EPS to $0.11-0.26 as 800G and 1.6T products ramp, and said demand exceeds capacity through mid-2027. A major new hyperscale customer deal was reported on 14 August, which is what carried the stock to roughly $149.52. Against that, the stock fell about 15% today to $131.41 and is down 23.3% over the 60-day window. The strongest counter-evidence is that adverse move, and this run traced it to the same sector-wide optics selloff that hit Lumentum, Corning and AXT on the same day, which reporting describes as macro rather than optics-specific, with the names that ran hardest giving back the most. That is a sentiment explanation rather than a disclosed change in the business, and because the read rests on a move this run can only attribute to rotation, it does not reach a clear net conviction — the disclosed guidance is what supports the position, not the tape.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $255M guidance floor, the new hyperscale customer arrangement is not confirmed in a company disclosure, or capacity constraints are disclosed as demand softening rather than a supply limit.

thesis: Micron is down 22.3% over the 60-day window and fell about 7-7.7% today. Two adverse items were found, one company-specific: Netlist filed a complaint with the U.S. International Trade Commission on 12 August against Micron, Super Micro, HPE and Lenovo alleging infringement of four patents tied to DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM products, seeking exclusion orders that would bar the allegedly infringing products from import into or sale in the United States rather than damages alone. The second is sector-wide: semiconductors under pressure from rising Treasury yields and concern over memory demand and pricing. The counter-case is that sell-side consensus remains Strong Buy on 29 buys and one hold, and that no company disclosure this run found revises Micron's own outlook. That does not settle the exclusion-order exposure, whose scope and timetable this run could not establish, so the evidence is genuinely offsetting.
invalidation: The ITC declines to institute an investigation, the parties settle, or Micron quantifies the DDR5 exposure as immaterial in a filing.

thesis: Rocket Lab is down 21.1% over the 60-day window despite a Q2 report that carried record revenue of $234.07M, up 62% year over year and about $3M above estimates, a record $2.36B backlog, a $397M U.S. Space Force Flatellites contract and a net loss narrowed to $0.08 per share, matching consensus. The offsetting disclosure came from the same report: stage-1 tank production still aligns with delivering Neutron to the launchpad in Q4 2026, but management stopped short of reaffirming a first flight before year end, balancing launch timing against scaling. The stock opened about 5% lower the next day on that timing language, and prediction-market pricing implies a low probability of a 2026 Neutron launch. A record commercial quarter and an unreaffirmed flight date for the vehicle the growth case rests on are directly offsetting, and this run cannot settle which dominates.
invalidation: Management reaffirms or abandons a 2026 Neutron first flight in a disclosure, or the Iridium acquisition closes and changes the revenue base.

thesis: Nebius reported Q2 2026 on 12 August with revenue of $582M, up 454% year over year, positive adjusted EBITDA of $236M and EPS of -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected, and reaffirmed full-year guidance of $3.0-3.4B revenue at a 40% EBITDA margin. The company disclosed four core AI cloud contracts averaging more than $1B each at yields of $20-25M per megawatt, and raised its year-end contracted power target to 5 gigawatts. Shares rose about 28% on the print and the stock is up 12.4% over the 60-day window, which is what tripped the screen. The strongest counter-evidence is the funding gap implied by the same guidance: capital expenditure of $20-25B against $3.0-3.4B of revenue. The company's answer, disclosed alongside the contracts, is that prepayments cover 50-60% of the associated capital expenditure, and it financed the earlier build with roughly $4.3B of convertible senior notes that closed in March 2026, structured with high conversion premiums to limit dilution. That covers part of the gap but not all of it, and no financing announced within the last ~90 days surfaced in this run's research, so the balance of the build remains unfunded as far as this run can establish.
invalidation: Full-year revenue guidance is cut below $3.0B, the contracted-power target is walked back, or a capital raise is announced on terms materially worse than the March convertible.

thesis: AMD is down 12.2% over the 60-day window. Its 4 August Q2 2026 report was internally mixed on the company's own numbers: revenue of $11.5B with GAAP gross margin of 54%, operating income of $2.0B, net income of $2.3B and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.38, with adjusted EPS of $1.66 — revenue and adjusted EPS both above estimates — while the 54% gross margin fell short of a 56% consensus on near-term costs from the Helios AI infrastructure ramp. Q3 revenue guidance was raised to a $13B midpoint and the Instinct MI400 series was launched. Shares fell 8-9% after hours on the margin line despite the revenue beat and the raise. Today's further decline came alongside Cerebras and Intel ahead of an unrelated industry event, which is sector movement rather than company news. A beat-and-raise offset by a margin miss the company attributes to its own build-out is exactly the kind of two-sided print this run cannot resolve into a clear net read before the next disclosure.
invalidation: Q3 gross margin recovers toward the 56% consensus level, or management quantifies the Helios ramp cost as ending on a stated timetable.

thesis: TSMC's July 2026 revenue was a record NT$467.58B, up 44.7% year over year and 5.6% above June, extending a run of 17.5%, 30.1% and 67.9% year-over-year gains in April, May and June. Management guides Q3 revenue to $44.6-45.8B with gross margin of 65-67%, has raised its 2026 outlook to revenue growth slightly above 40% in dollar terms and lifted capital spending to $60-64B. Against that disclosed record, the stock is down 11.6% over the 60-day window and sits about 13-14% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is that this drawdown coincides with a broad semiconductor derating driven by rising Treasury yields and doubts about AI infrastructure financing rather than by anything TSMC disclosed — the same rotation visible across Micron, Marvell and AMD today. Because the read on the price move rests on that macro attribution rather than on a company disclosure, it is not a settled explanation, and the position case rests on the monthly revenue disclosures alone.
invalidation: A monthly revenue report comes in below the prior-year comparable, or Q3 revenue or gross margin lands under the guided ranges.

thesis: Cerebras tripped the screen on volume — 2.13x the prior 30-bar average — rather than price, and fell about 12.6-13.7% today from Monday's $251.98 close, erasing the prior session's 15.1% gain. The Q2 print reported on 12 August is two-sided on the company's own figures: core revenue up 103% and cloud revenue nearly quadrupled, guidance raised, but GAAP revenue was reduced by OpenAI warrant accounting and the company swung to a quarterly loss. Management also warned that renting back AI compute from an existing customer while its own data centres come online will weigh on gross margins. Today's decline came ahead of the 6:30pm ET 'Supernova' event expected to launch the WSE-4 processor, which reporting characterises as a buy-the-rumour, sell-the-news setup layered on a macro rotation, compounded by roughly 36.4 million shares becoming eligible for sale around 14 August. A guidance raise sitting alongside a GAAP revenue reduction, a swing to a loss, a disclosed margin headwind and a share overhang is unresolved evidence, and the pipeline's own prior cycle already misread this name by quoting only its favourable revenue metric.
invalidation: The WSE-4 launch converts into disclosed customer commitments, or the compute rent-back margin headwind is quantified and bounded in a company disclosure.

thesis: Held position, re-screened fresh. Microsoft's Q4 fiscal 2026 report disclosed revenue of $90.01B, up 18% from $76.44B, and adjusted EPS of $4.74 against a $4.21 consensus, with Azure growth accelerating to 43% and annual cloud revenue passing $100B alongside record commercial remaining performance obligations. The stock is up 31.1% over the 60-day window and sits 12.8% below its 52-week high; the account's position is modestly underwater against a $503.62 average cost. The strongest counter-evidence is legal and structural rather than operational: securities class actions naming the company and four officers allege that disclosures understated the concentration risk of Azure's AI-driven growth depending on a small number of large language model partners, after Microsoft invested over $13B in OpenAI and committed up to $5B to Anthropic while those partners committed to large Azure purchases, and Elon Musk is separately seeking $79B-$134B from OpenAI and Microsoft. What limits that counter-case is its scope: the complaints contest the adequacy of disclosure about concentration, not the reported revenue or Azure growth figures themselves, and the only scheduled date this run found — an 11 August lead-plaintiff deadline — has already passed, with no hearing, ruling or compliance date inside the next ~90 days surfacing. What it does not settle is whether the growth is durable if partner spending slows, which is the substance of the allegation and remains open.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates materially in the next quarterly disclosure, a court sets a near-term merits date or the company discloses a reserve, or Microsoft discloses a change in the OpenAI or Anthropic commercial arrangements.
sources: National Law Review (securities class action notice): https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/msft-shareholder-alert-august-11-2026-lead-plaintiff-deadline-microsoft

thesis: Held position, re-screened fresh. Astera Labs reported Q2 2026 after the close on 4 August with record revenue of $392.4M, up 27% sequentially and 104% year over year on AI fabric and signal-conditioning demand, EPS of $0.80 against a $0.69 consensus, and Q3 EPS guidance of $1.16-1.21 against a $0.81 consensus — a guide well above where the street sat. Citi, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies all raised price targets after the print. Against that, the stock is down 31.0% over the 60-day window and sits 39.4% below its 52-week high, and the account's position is underwater against a $323.92 average cost. That is a large adverse move with no disclosed deterioration behind it, and this run traced it to the same broad de-rating of AI infrastructure names visible across Marvell, Micron, AMD and the optics group — rising Treasury yields and caution on AI capital spending, not company news. No litigation or regulatory matter naming Astera Labs turned up. The read is therefore that the disclosed results still support holding while the price move is a sector repricing this run can attribute but not resolve, which is not a clear net read on the stock itself.
invalidation: Q3 revenue or EPS lands below the guided range, a major hyperscaler design win is disclosed as lost, or the sequential growth rate breaks.
sources: 24/7 Wall St. (18 August AI hardware rotation): https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/cerebras-intel-and-amd-shares-fall-ahead-of-tonights-supernova-event/

thesis: Held position, re-screened fresh. Coherent reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 12 August with revenue of $2.05B, up 33.8% year over year, beating on both lines and guiding above expectations on AI optical-networking demand. Both margin measures were disclosed and they differ: GAAP gross margin 38.5% with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.19, non-GAAP gross margin 40.2% with non-GAAP EPS of $1.74. On 17 August the company began customer sampling of 300mm high-thermal-conductivity silicon carbide substrates with AI semiconductor partners, moving that platform from internal development into customer evaluation. Against that, the stock fell about 12.8% today and is down 28.0% over the 60-day window, sitting 30.5% below its 52-week high; the account's position is underwater against a $338.53 average cost. This run traced today's drop to a sector-wide optics selloff — Lumentum down about 10%, Corning about 8%, AXT about 12.5% — which reporting describes as largely macro in origin, noting nothing changed in the indium phosphide picture within 24 hours and that the names which ran hardest into the day gave back the most. Nothing found points to a disclosed deterioration at Coherent, but a drawdown this size explained only by rotation is not a settled read, so the position is supported by the disclosed results rather than by the tape.
invalidation: The next quarterly guidance is cut, non-GAAP gross margin falls back below the high-30s, or the 300mm SiC customer evaluations are disclosed as not progressing.
sources: StockTitan (Coherent FY2026 Q4 results timing and coverage): https://www.stocktitan.net/news/COHR/coherent-corp-announces-timing-of-fy2026-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-02fo7c2uxxlb.html

thesis: Held position, re-screened fresh. Dell's disclosed AI server position is the strongest in the account: fiscal Q1 revenue up 88% with AI-optimised server revenue of $16.1B, up 757%, a $24.4B AI order booked in the quarter and an AI server backlog of $51.3B, which management used to raise its fiscal 2027 AI server goal to $60B from $50B and to set total fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $165-169B. The stock is up 11.9% over the 60-day window, closed near $484.50 on 12 August on read-through from CoreWeave and Super Micro results, and now sits 9.5% below its 52-week high; the account's position is modestly underwater against a $497.02 average cost. The strongest counter-evidence is timing rather than substance: the next earnings report is scheduled for 3 September, inside the likely holding window, and it is the first check on whether the raised $60B AI target and the $165-169B revenue goal survive contact with actual conversion of that backlog. Nothing this run found disputes the backlog figure, but an unresolved binary that close caps the rating regardless of how the disclosed numbers read.
invalidation: The 3 September report shows AI server backlog shrinking, the $60B fiscal 2027 AI goal is walked back, or AI server gross margin is disclosed as deteriorating as volume scales.
